content: The EMT-Critical Care certification is a specific level of Emergency Medical Services (EMS) certification that is exclusive to New York State. The education and scope of practice for EMT-Critical Care are very similar to those of the National Standard EMT-Intermediate certification. Individuals with this certification are authorized to perform advanced medical procedures, including endotracheal intubation, intravenous (IV) therapy, cardiac monitoring, and electrical therapies. They are also trained to perform needle thoracotomy and cricothyrotomy, as well as administer medications. Compared to paramedics, EMT-Critical Care providers generally have fewer diagnostic capabilities and, as a result, operate under fewer standing orders. However, they are trained to perform all the same medical procedures as paramedics.
